title: Mass spectrometry
examples: How does mass spectrometry help us find unknown chemicals?
What is the difference between the molecular ion peak and a fragment peak?
Can you explain what the mass-to-charge ratio really means?

explain.say: Today we learn about mass spectrometry for finding things.
The first key step creates a molecular ion, which is the whole molecule plus a charge.
Sometimes the molecular ion breaks apart in a process called fragmentation.
The mass-to-charge ratio, or m over z, tells us the mass of the piece.
In a real lab, we use this to identify unknown drugs or pollutants.
A common mistake is assuming the molecular ion is always the biggest peak.

items: The largest peak is not always the molecular ion.
Fragmentation can create a larger peak.
Always look for the M+ peak specifically.

faq.q: What is the difference between the molecular ion and a fragment ion?
faq.a: The molecular ion represents the intact molecule that has lost just one electron. A fragment ion is a smaller piece that has broken off the original molecule.
asks: How do I tell which peak is which?
Are fragment ions always smaller than the molecular ion?

faq.q: Why is the mass-to-charge ratio important?
faq.a: It allows us to calculate the actual mass of the particle by dividing its measured mass by its charge. This gives us a unique identifier for the substance.
asks: Does the charge affect the mass reading?

faq.q: Does the energy used in the machine affect the results?
faq.a: Yes, the energy level controls how much fragmentation occurs. More energy causes more breaking, which changes the spectrum.
asks: What if I use too much energy?

faq.a: Yes, it can detect different isotopes by measuring slight variations in mass. For example, carbon-12 versus carbon-13.
asks: Can it see different versions of the same element?

faq.q: Is the molecular ion peak always present?
faq.a: No, depending on the molecule's stability and the ionization energy used, the molecular ion peak might not appear at all.
asks: What if the molecule breaks up completely?
Is it guaranteed to see M+?

facts: Mass spectrometry measures the mass-to-charge ratio of ions.
The molecular ion (M+.) represents the intact molecule minus one electron.
Fragmentation occurs when the molecular ion breaks into smaller, charged pieces.
The resulting pattern of peaks is called a mass spectrum.

quiz.say: If a molecule has a mass of 100 and carries a charge of plus one, what is its m/z ratio?
quiz.why: The ratio is calculated by dividing the mass by the charge, giving 100.

wrong.0: This incorrectly subtracts the charge instead of dividing by it.
wrong.1: This only considers the charge and ignores the actual mass.
wrong.3: This incorrectly adds the charge instead of dividing by it.

quiz.say: What process causes a large molecule to break into smaller ions?
quiz.why: Fragmentation is the specific term for the process where the ion breaks into smaller pieces.

wrong.1: Ionization is the initial step of adding the charge, not the breaking apart.
wrong.2: Acceleration is the physical movement of the ion through the machine.
wrong.3: Detection is simply measuring the resulting ions, not causing the break.

quiz.say: When analyzing a substance, which peak usually corresponds to the original, whole molecule?

options.show: The peak with the smallest m/z
options.say: The peak with the smallest m/z

quiz.why: The molecular ion peak represents the mass of the molecule before it breaks apart.

wrong.0: This peak usually represents a single proton or electron, not the whole molecule.
wrong.2: While often true, the highest mass peak is not guaranteed to be the molecular ion.
wrong.3: The smallest m/z peak is usually a very small fragment, not the whole molecule.
